'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****[[United Nations]] representative for [[Afghanistan]] [[Deborah Lyons]] implores the [[Afghan government]] and the [[Taliban]] to protect civilians as a UN report shows a sharp increase in civilians being killed. 1,300 civilians, mostly women and children, have been killed so far this year. [https://www.dw.com/en/un-warns-of-spike-in-afghan-civilian-deaths/a-58640128 (DW)]
****Forty-six [[Afghan National Army]] soldiers, including five [[Officer (armed forces)|officers]], flee into neighbouring [[Pakistan]] after abandoning their military posts on [[Afghanistan–Pakistan border|the border]] amid Taliban advances. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2312190/another-group-of-afghan-military-personnel-given-refuge-by-army-ispr (''The Express Tribune'')]
*[[American-led intervention in Iraq (2014–present)|American-led intervention in Iraq]]
**[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq (2020–2021)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] announces that U.S. combat forces will leave [[Iraq]] by the end of the year, although some [[United States Army|troops]] will remain to "train and advise" the [[Iraqi Armed Forces|Iraqi military]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-57970464 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Tunisian political crisis]]
**The [[Tunisian Army|army]] surrounds the [[Assembly of the Representatives of the People|parliament]] and prevents its [[Speaker of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People|Speaker]] [[Rached Ghannouchi]] from entering. [[President of Tunisia|President]] [[Kais Saied]] earlier dismissed [[Prime Minister of Tunisia|Prime Minister]] [[Hichem Mechichi]] and froze the activities of the parliament for 30 days. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/tunisian-army-stops-speaker-entering-parliament-witness-says-2021-07-26/ (Reuters)]
**Police storm and raid the headquarters of news outlet [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] in [[Tunis]], as clashes continue outside the building. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/26/tunisia-police-storm-al-jazeera-office-in-tunis (Al Jazeera)]
**The main opposition [[Islamism|Islamist]] [[Ennahda Movement]] accuses President Saied of staging a [[Coup d'état|coup]] as clashes between the President's supporters and Islamist protesters continue in the capital [[Tunis]]. An Ennahda office is burned down in the city of [[Tozeur]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-57976005 (BBC News)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**Five soldiers and a civilian are killed and four more people are wounded as [[Boko Haram]] attack a command post in Zigue, [[Cameroon]]. A number of terrorist are killed during a gunfight after the attack. [https://www.thedefensepost.com/2021/07/28/boko-haram-cameroon-attack/amp/ (''The Defense Post'')]
*[[Insurgency in Northeast India]]
**Five policemen are killed and more than 50 people are wounded in the [[Indian state]] of [[Assam]] during clashes with [[Mizoram]] due to a [[border dispute]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/26/six-police-1-civilian-killed-in-clash-between-two-indian-states (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Madagascar food crisis]]
**[[USAID]] announces a donation of [[United States dollar|$]]7.5 million for feeding and treating children and pregnant women in southern [[Madagascar]]. The country is experiencing its worst [[drought]] in the past 40 years, with more than one million people on the verge of [[famine]]. [https://mg.usembassy.gov/100000-people-in-southern-madagascar-to-benefit-from-new-u-s-government-assistance/ (US embassy Madagascar)]
*Thirteen people are killed and 45 others are injured when a long-distance bus rolls over on the [[G22 Qingdao–Lanzhou Expressway]] in [[Gansu]], [[China]]. This is the second major disaster in the province this year after the [[Gansu ultramarathon disaster]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/2021-07/26/c_1127697562.htm (Xinhua News Agency)]
*A [[dust storm]] causes a 20-vehicle pileup on [[Interstate 15]] in the [[U.S. state]] of [[Utah]], killing eight people and injuring several others, some of whom are in critical condition, according to a statement from the [[Utah Highway Patrol]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/07/26/us/utah-sandstorm-multi-vehicle-crash/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/jul/26/killed-in-20-car-pileup-in-utah-sandstorm (''The Guardian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in South Korea]]
*****[[South Korea]] begins [[vaccination|vaccinations]] for people between the ages of 55 and 59 as the country experiences a fourth wave of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/south-korea-covid-19-start-vaccine-55-59-age-group-15296874 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 15,192 new cases and 247 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.179 million and the nationwide death toll to 19,521. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/27/bangladesh-record-coronavirus-cases-deaths (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] eases their [[Community Activities Restrictions Enforcement|community activities restrictions]] and allows non-essential [[traditional market]]s, [[warung]]s, [[Street food of Indonesia|street food]] vendors, and some shopping malls as well as other small businesses to reopen with strict health measures despite warnings that further loosening could contribute to another wave of COVID-19. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jul/26/indonesia-loosens-covid-restrictions-despite-record-deaths (''The Guardian'')]
****Indonesia reports a record 40,374 recoveries from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 2.54 million. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5657353/rekor-kasus-sembuh-covid-26-juli-di-ri-tambah-40374-kasus-baru-28228?tag_from=news_mostpop (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 31,814 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours,  bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3.72 million.  [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/iran-records-highest-single-day-covid-19-cases-since-outbreak/2314491 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan]]
****[[Kazakhstan]] reports a record 6,637 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 535,906.  [https://m.akipress.com/news:660890:Kazakhstan_reports_6,637_daily_new_coronavirus_cases/ (AKIPress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 207 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 8,201.  [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/malaysia-reports-record-207-new-coronavirus-deaths (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 15,376 new cases of COVID-19, and surpasses 500,000 cases of the virus.  [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2154859/record-15-376-new-covid-cases (''Bangkok Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Ho Chi Minh City]] imposes a strict overnight curfew from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/vietnam-s-economic-hub-imposes-night-curfew-as-country-battles-virus-surge (Radio France Internationale)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia]]
****[[Croatia]] restricts the number of gatherings to 50 people for those who are unvaccinated and 1,000 people for those who are [[COVID-19 vaccination in Croatia|vaccinated]] in five coastal [[Counties of Croatia|counties]] in [[Adriatic Croatia]] until August 15 in order to prevent the introduction of restrictions for travellers returning from the country. [https://www.croatiaweek.com/croatia-tightens-covid-restrictions-along-adriatic-coast/ (Croatia Week)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****Pubs and restaurants are allowed to resume their indoor service across [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] for the first time since March 2020, although customers must have official proof that they have been fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Republic of Ireland|vaccinated]] or have recovered from COVID-19 within the last 180 days. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-57965158.amp (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] approves the clinical trial of the combined [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|AstraZeneca]] and [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] COVID-19 vaccine. [https://news.yahoo.com/russia-approves-trials-combined-astrazeneca-191424514.html (Yahoo! News)]   
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[United States Department of Veterans Affairs|U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs]] announces that they will require vaccinations for healthcare workers, becoming the first agency to do so. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/26/us/politics/veterans-affairs-coronavirus-covid-19.html (''The New York Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the San Francisco Bay Area]]
*****Bars and nightclubs in [[San Francisco]] will require [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccinations]] or a negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test]] for customers as an effort to combat the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://sanfrancisco.cbslocal.com/2021/07/26/san-francisco-bars-covid-vaccine-sf-bar-owner-alliance/ (KPIX-TV)]
****[[California]] announces that the state will mandate COVID-19 vaccines for healthcare workers, becoming the first [[U.S. state]] to do so. [https://www.dailynews.com/2021/07/26/california-to-require-vaccination-proof-for-health-workers/ (''Los Angeles Daily Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria]]
***[[Algeria]] closes gyms, cultural and leisure venues, beaches and used car markets, reimposes a curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m., and bans all gatherings in 35 [[Provinces of Algeria|province]]s, amid the rapid spread of the Delta variant. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/algeria-reimposes-restrictions-gatherings-stem-coronavirus-cases-2021-07-25/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
***[[Venezuela]] enters a "radical [[quarantine]]" for a week in order to reduce the spread of the Delta variant of COVID-19. [https://www.elconfidencial.com/mundo/2021-07-26/venezuela-cuarentena-radical-azote-variante-delta-covid19-coronavirus_3201471/ (''El Confidencial'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Equatorial Guinea]]
**The Foreign Minister of [[Equatorial Guinea]] announces the closure of the country's [[Embassy of Equatorial Guinea, London|embassy]] in [[London]], [[United Kingdom]] after the British government sanctioned Vice-President [[Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue]] over his "lavish lifestyle". The Minister said that Equatorial Guinea "will not allow interference in internal affairs". [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/equatorial-guinea-close-embassy-london-2021-07-26/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
**The [[French Parliament]] approves a law that requires all [[healthcare worker]]s to receive a [[COVID-19 vaccination in France|vaccine]] by September 15 as well as the adoption of a "Health Pass" that will allow residents to travel on trains and airplanes, and enter restaurants and some public venues. The law can be applied until November 15 depending on the COVID-19 situation and will also apply to children over the age of 12 beginning on September 30. [https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210725-french-parliament-approves-law-requiring-restaurant-covid-pass-vaccine-rules (France 24)] 

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Iranian protests]]
**Protests against water shortages and deteriorating economic condition have spread to capital [[Tehran]], as protesters openly display discontent with the country's leadership. [https://www.rferl.org/a/tehran-protests-death-dictator/31378061.html (Radio Farda)]
*[[2020–21 Malaysian political crisis]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**The [[Parliament of Malaysia]] reopens for the first time after a seven-month suspension due to the COVID-19-related [[2021 Malaysian state of emergency|state of emergency]], which will expire on August 1. [https://asia.nikkei.com/Politics/Malaysia-in-transition/Malaysia-parliament-battle-resumes-with-Muhyiddin-in-hot-seat (''Nikkei Asia'')]
*[[Mary Simon]] is officially sworn in as the 30th [[governor general of Canada]]. She is the first [[Indigenous peoples in Canada|Indigenous]] person to hold the office. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/mary-simon-installed-as-governor-general-1.6114622 (CBC)]
*[[Najib Mikati]] is designated by the [[Parliament of Lebanon|Lebanese parliament]] to be the new [[Prime Minister of Lebanon|prime minister]], succeeding caretaker prime minister [[Hassan Diab]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/lebanese-president-meets-businessman-mikati-set-be-designated-premier-2021-07-26/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020 Summer Olympics]]
**[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[Netherlands at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
***The Dutch rowing team self-isolates after rower [[Finn Florijn]] and team coach Josy Verdonkschot tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.barrons.com/amp/news/netherlands-olympics-rowing-team-self-isolates-after-virus-cases-01627277107 (''Barron's'')]
**[[Philippines at the 2020 Summer Olympics]], [[Weightlifting at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Filipinos|Filipino]] [[Olympic weightlifting|weightlifter]] [[Hidilyn Diaz]] wins the [[Weightlifting at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's 55 kg|Women's 55 kg event]], receiving the [[Philippines at the Olympics|Philippines' first-ever Olympic gold medal]]. [https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/weightlifting-diaz-wins-first-ever-olympic-gold-philippines-2021-07-26/ (Reuters)]
